text: The framework begins with graph construction and depth confidence measurement to process the input stereo data.
First, the input RGB image is abstracted into homogeneous superpixels using the Simple Linear Iterative Clustering algorithm.
Concurrently, the depth distribution is analyzed using mean depth, variation, and frequency entropy to compute a depth confidence measure.
The superpixel graph and depth confidence score are then routed into two complementary saliency stages.
In Stage 1, compactness saliency is calculated by evaluating the spatial spread of color and depth cues alongside objectness scores.
A depth-refined foreground seed selection mechanism filters preliminary seeds using compactness saliency and mean depth values.
In Stage 2, foreground saliency is computed by measuring multi-cue contrast —including color, depth, texture, and position—against the selected seeds.
The compactness and foreground saliency maps are integrated through a weighted summation to leverage their complementary strengths.
The aggregated result is then normalized to generate the final prediction.
The resulting saliency map accurately highlights the salient object, demonstrating close agreement with the ground truth annotation.
